A large and disorganized tropical disturbance is located northeast 
of Saipan and is producing isolated to numerous, locally heavy 
showers and isolated thunderstorms. This system is expected to move 
just north of the Marianas over the next day. A col remains over the 
CNMI that is keeping winds light. However, a developing monsoonal 
flow into the system is expected to increase the winds beginning 
tonight over all islands. Sustained winds of 15 to 25 mph will be 
possible with gusts of 30 mph. Guam will be more likely to receive 
higher winds and heavier showers. The unstable airmass and high 
precipitable water values may allow for heavy showers to develop, 
creating a potential flooding risk. The monsoon flow is expected to 
be strongest over Guam but high uncertainty remains in where the 
highest rainfall amounts will occur and there may be breaks between 
instances of heavy rainfall. By Friday, drier, more stable air will 
bring a short period of just isolated showers. Another trough is 
likely to move into the region over the weekend bringing more 
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms. Periods of isolated to 
scattered showers are expected to continue early next week.

Marine...
Combined seas of 5 to 6 feet are expected to rise significantly 
through Thursday night, reaching as high as 8 to 9 feet across Guam 
coastal waters due to a strengthening west and southwesterly monsoon 
surge. Light to moderate winds may also increase by Thursday with 
maximum sustained winds of 25 knots and gusts up to 30 knots. 
Therefore, seas may also reach or near criteria hazardous to small 
craft by sometime Thursday. The monsoon surge will bring the 
potential for numerous locally heavy showers and isolated 
thunderstorms through at least Thursday night with somewhat lower 
shower coverage for the northern CNMI.

There is a moderate risk of rip currents along west, north, and 
south- facing reefs as a spread of swells from the southwest to the 
northwest continues to increase. South facing reefs will build 
Thursday over Guam sooner than the northern CNMI. Hazardous surf is 
expected to develop along west-facing reefs so a high surf advisory 
has been issued beginning Thursday. West facing reefs may reach a 
high risk for rip currents by Thursday as the swell builds in and 
winds become elevated. There will be a moderate risk of lightning 
through at least Thursday night.

Tropical Systems...
Tropical Depression Krovanh (22W) is centered near 23N133E, 
southeast of Okinawa and is currently moving to northwest at around 
9 mph. It is expected to maintain this course with a slight increase 
in forward speed through Thursday. Maximum sustained winds remain at 
35 mph. Krovanh is forecast to intensify slightly through Thursday, 
potentially returning to Tropical Storm status before noon on 
Thursday as it approaches the Ryukyu Islands. The system is expected 
to meander along the northwest fringes of National Weather Service 
(NWS) Guam's Area of Responsibility, with no direct impacts expected 
to any of our forecast points. For more information on Tropical 
Depression Krovanh, see bulletins from JTWC under WMO header WTPN31 
PGTW, and public advisories from the NWS under WMO header WTPQ31 
PGUM. 

Eastern Micronesia...
The weather in Eastern Micronesia is being dominated by the monsoon 
trough, which is quite unusual. However, this is an unusual year, 
with a 90 percent chance of a very strong El Nino, and a 69 percent 
chance of having one of the strongest recorded since 1950.

There is a speed change feature within the monsoon flow, where the 
flow speeds up, creating a region of divergence, then slows down 
again on the other side, creating a region of convergence. This is 
creating a band of showers which is now exiting Majuro and heading 
toward Kosrae. Meanwhile, leftover debris cloudiness is gradually 
thinning over Pohnpei.

As the speed change feature departs Majuro, look for relatively 
sunny skies through Friday, and only isolated showers through 
Saturday. Winds will be 5 to 10 knots through Sunday, then could 
pick up a bit on Monday. Seas will be 3 to 5 feet through Sunday, 
then could rise to between 4 and 6 feet Monday. This will lead to a 
continuation of the benign marine conditions that have been enjoyed 
recently. Start conserving water now though, a drought is likely 
coming by next year.

As the speed change feature approaches Kosrae, look for isolated 
showers becoming scattered by Thursday, and could last through 
Friday night. Saturday and Sunday will see a return to drier 
weather, then it could moisten again Monday. Winds will be 5 to 10 
knots, primarily from the west or northwest. Seas will be 4 to 6 
feet. This will lead a continuation of the benign marine conditions 
here also. Likewise, start conserving water now, a drought is likely 
coming by next year.
